answer: Unique-work audit trail. Each identity must submit a distinct, verifiable work artifact before transacting; duplicates, including near-copies, are rejected by comparing a nebula-derived embedding of the artifact. Approval also draws one random marble from a shared pool, and every failed draw adds a pigment token charge to the submitter. A clone therefore pays full submission cost for a likely-rejected artifact, plus repeated draw charges, while yielding no new capacity—making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
